myth_of_the_day_pool.statement: “You shouldn’t exercise or play during your period.”
myth_of_the_day_pool.explanation: Gentle movement often eases cramps. Dance, play, stretch, whatever feels good for you.

myth_of_the_day_pool.statement: “Once your periods start, you stop growing taller.”
myth_of_the_day_pool.explanation: Growth slows down, but most girls still grow a few more centimetres after their first period.

myth_of_the_day_pool.statement: “During your period you’ll spoil pickle if you touch it.”
myth_of_the_day_pool.explanation: Periods can’t spoil food. This belief has no science behind it at all.

myth_of_the_day_pool.statement: “You shouldn’t bathe or wash your hair during your period.”
myth_of_the_day_pool.explanation: A warm bath keeps you fresh and can even ease cramps.

myth_of_the_day_pool.statement: “Girls can’t use tampons or cups until they’re grown up.”
myth_of_the_day_pool.explanation: Teens can use them too, when they feel ready and know how. Many girls start with pads first.

myth_of_the_day_pool.statement: “It’s fine to flush a pad if you’re in a hurry.”
myth_of_the_day_pool.explanation: Pads swell up and block pipes. Always wrap and bin, even in a hurry.
When everyone understands periods, there’s less teasing and more support.

myth_of_the_day_pool.statement: “Pain that makes you miss school every month is just normal.”
myth_of_the_day_pool.explanation: Strong pain is worth checking with a doctor. You don’t have to just put up with it.

myth_of_the_day_pool.statement: “If you have a menstrual disorder, you did something wrong.”
myth_of_the_day_pool.explanation: These conditions are nobody’s fault. Doctors can help you feel better.

myth_of_the_day_pool.statement: “Only girls who aren’t clean get infections.”
myth_of_the_day_pool.explanation: Anyone can get one. Infections are common, treatable and nothing to be ashamed of.

myth_of_the_day_pool.statement: “Telling an adult about bullying is snitching.”
myth_of_the_day_pool.explanation: Telling is getting help. Adults can do things kids can’t.
Sometimes it can be someone a child knows. That’s why every child can say no and tell, about anyone.
Anyone can report, including a child, a parent or a teacher.
Even best friends disagree. What matters is how you sort it out.
Crying is a healthy way to let feelings out. Brave people feel things too.
